requirement.summary: Report - TMS039 - Add Syndicate Owner Indicator field
requirement.description:
User Story

As a report user, I want the "Syndicate Owner Indicator" field added to the TMS039 Override Date Limitation for Advance Booking report so that I can identify each reservation's syndicate owner status at a glance.

Current Behavior

The TMS039 Override Date Limitation for Advance Booking report does not display the "Syndicate Owner Indicator" field. The value is stored in the TMS reservation record (DB field hkjc_resv_members: rmem_syndicate_owner_indicator, ref. HERO-64070, HERO-67705) but is not surfaced in this report.

Expected Behavior

The TMS039 Override Date Limitation for Advance Booking report should display a new "Syndicate Owner Indicator" column placed to the LEFT of the "Syndicate Owner" field. The column should render the following values from the database:

- Y = Yes → display "Y"

- N = No → display "N"

- empty = reservation uses an offline profile with no Syndicate Owner Indicator → display blank

The field must be visible to all users who can currently access this report, and must appear in both the on-screen display and all printed/exported formats (e.g., PDF, Excel).

Acceptance Criteria

Add Syndicate Owner Indicator column

- Given the user opens the TMS039 Override Date Limitation for Advance Booking report

- When the report is generated

- Then a new column named "Syndicate Owner Indicator" is displayed to the LEFT of the "Syndicate Owner" field

- And the column is visible to all users who can currently access this report

- And the column appears in the on-screen display and in all printed/exported formats (PDF, Excel)

Display indicator values

- Given a reservation has a Syndicate Owner Indicator value in the database

- When the report is generated

- Then the cell displays "Y" when the DB value is Y

- And the cell displays "N" when the DB value is N

- But the cell is left blank when the DB value is empty (reservation uses an offline profile with no Syndicate Owner Indicator)

Handle unexpected DB values

- Given the DB field hkjc_resv_members: rmem_syndicate_owner_indicator contains a value other than Y, N, or empty (e.g., null, whitespace, or an unexpected character)

- When the report is generated

- Then the cell is left blank and the report does not error or crash

Supporting Evidence

DB field: hkjc_resv_members: rmem_syndicate_owner_indicator (to be confirmed with TMS team)

Related tickets: HERO-64070, HERO-67705 (Syndicate Owner Indicator field added to TMS reservation record)

Requested Timeline

Aligned with Priority: Medium

Notes: No fixed deadline provided by requester.

Original Description (preserved by INF Prod. Studio)

Background

Syndicate Owner Indicator field is added to TMS reservation record (ref. HERO-64070, HERO-67705). It is also needed to show in several reports.

Requirement

In the 10 reports below,

| TMS009 Special Booking List (By Outlet)

| TMS015 Pre-Race Booking List

| TMS016 Post-Race Booking List

| TMS020 Waiting List Report

| TMS022 Master Pre-Race Booking List

| TMS024 Waiting List Extraction

| TMS025 Unsuccessful Waiting List Report (By Outlet)

| TMS035 Waiting List Report (Owner Box)

| TMS037 Master Pre-Race Booking List with Contact Information

| TMS039 Override Date Limitation for Advance Booking

To add "Syndicate Owner Indicator" field on the LEFT of "Syndicate Owner” field.

requirement.summary: Report - POS015 Discount Report By Check - Apply decimal place and thousands separator per Report Format Configuration
requirement.description:
User Story

As a report user, I want the POS015 Discount Report By Check to format the Item Department column values according to the active Report Format Configuration (Decimal Place and Thousand Separator) so that the report output is consistent, accurate, and readable across all output formats and environments.

Current Behavior

The POS015 Discount Report By Check on both HQ and Local currently displays numeric values in the Item Department columns with decimal places (e.g., trailing zeros) and fails to apply thousands separators, even though the configuration has been set up under System Configuration > Report Module. The report ignores the configured Decimal Place and Thousand Separator settings.

Expected Behavior

The POS015 Discount Report By Check should format all numeric values in the Item Department columns based on the active Report Format Configuration under System Configuration > Report Module. The formatting must respect the exact decimal-place count defined in the configuration (e.g., a setting of 2 keeps 10.50 as 10.50; a setting of 0 removes all decimals) and apply thousands separators when enabled. The same formatting must be applied identically across all output formats (on-screen, PDF, Excel/CSV) and must behave identically whether generated from HQ or Local, since both read from the same Report Format Configuration. Only newly generated reports reflect configuration changes; previously saved or exported reports remain unchanged.

Acceptance Criteria

Apply decimal place and thousands separator formatting to Item Department columns

- Given the Report Format Configuration under System Configuration > Report Module defines a Decimal Place count and a Thousand Separator setting

- When the POS015 Discount Report By Check is generated

- Then all numeric values in the Item Department columns are displayed with exactly the configured decimal-place count

- And thousands separators are applied to all relevant numeric values when the Thousand Separator setting is enabled

- But if the Thousand Separator setting is disabled, no thousands separators are applied

- But if the Decimal Place count is set to 0, all decimal places are removed (e.g., 10.50 becomes 11 when rounded, or 10 when truncated per existing rounding rules)

Consistent formatting across all output formats

- Given the Report Format Configuration is set

- When the POS015 Discount Report By Check is generated in any output format (on-screen, PDF, Excel/CSV)

- Then the decimal place and thousands separator formatting is applied identically across all output formats

- But if any output format cannot render the configured formatting, the report still displays the value without corrupting or dropping the underlying numeric data

Identical behavior on HQ and Local

- Given the POS015 Discount Report By Check is generated from either the HQ backend or a local store terminal

- When both environments read from the same Report Format Configuration

- Then both HQ and Local produce identical formatted output for the same underlying data

Configuration changes apply to newly generated reports only

- Given the Report Format Configuration is modified

- When a new POS015 Discount Report By Check is generated after the change

- Then the new report reflects the updated formatting

- And previously saved or exported reports remain unchanged

- But if a report is regenerated after the configuration change, it reflects the new formatting

Supporting Evidence

Report module current configuration sample provided in the original ticket.

Requested Timeline

Aligned with Priority: Medium

Preferred Quarter: Not specified

Target Version: Not specified

Notes: Scope is strictly limited to the POS015 Discount Report By Check; other reports will be handled in separate tickets.

Alternatives Considered

Not specified by requester.

POS015 Discount Report by Check

Support to follow the setting: System Configuration>Report Module>Format Configuration>'Decimal Place' & 'Thousand Separator'

Ticket ID: #1811112

Subject: TR: incorrect passerby file format

Department: Infrasys Support

URL: https://support-intl.shijigroup.com/agent/shijigroupintl/infrasys-support/tickets/details/255139000965682341

Case Description

vendor: gc_passerby_export

The content format in the passerby file "SLPR_POS1_20260401_5.zip" is incorrect, and the errors maybe caused by the following situations:

1. The title appears multiple times.

2. The content appears multiple times.

3. Wrong unzip password.

4. The POS code has not been configured in Book360.
requirement.release_notes:
Bug fixing: [Jira-67731] incorrect passerby file format
Description:
-      The gc_passerby_export interface produced an incorrect passerby ZIP/LST file format (sample file: SLPR_POS1_20260401_5.zip).
-      Symptoms included duplicated title/header lines, duplicated content rows, failure to unzip with the configured password, and Book360 rejecting the POS code.
-      Root cause: the LST file was always opened in append mode and the ZIP archive was created without overwrite, so a retry or leftover local file duplicated the header and rows; ZIP encryption used AES-256, which many unzip tools treat as a wrong password; POS_Code was written as the outlet name instead of the Outlet Mapping value.
Configuration / Parameter:
-      No special configuration or parameter is required.
-      Ensure Additional Setup > Outlet Mapping is configured as [outlet_code],[Book360 POS code] so POS_Code is exported correctly.
Field Definition:
-      This case does not involve field definition.
Result / Sample:
-      Before:
-      The exported passerby file could contain duplicated headers/content, and the ZIP could not be unzipped correctly with the configured password.
-      After:
-      The export file can be generated correctly, and duplicated headers and unzip failures no longer occur.
